title: Complete ordinary-prime counting compensation and the exact scale of its actual-source PNT envelope

sections.title: Exact ordinary-prime summation with the lower endpoint at two
sections.proof:
Keep the fixed source and all notation from the higher-power budget: D_L(theta)=E_o-aE_e, k_L(t)=D_L(1-t/L), h_L(t)=exp(-t/2)k_L(t), L>=1, a=No/Ne, beta=L^2/(16pi^2), d0=175/(88pi^2). In particular h_L(0)=h_L(L)=0. All t derivatives below hold L fixed. Let b=log2, Pi(t)=pi(exp t), and ell(t)=0 for t<b, ell(t)=integral_b^t exp(u)/u du for t>=b. Set Delta_pi=Pi-ell, extended by0 below b. Delta_pi(b)=1: the actual first-prime jump is included, not declared zero.

The COMPLETE ordinary-prime source is exactly
 B1(L)=-sum_(p<=exp L)log(p)p^(-1/2)k_L(log p)
      =-integral_b^L exp(t)h_L(t)dt
        +integral_b^L Delta_pi(t)[t h_L(t)]'dt.             (1)
Use the left endpoint b-minus in Stieltjes summation: Delta_pi(b-minus)=0, while the jump at b remains inside the measure. The upper atom also remains included; its source value is zero because k_L(L)=0. No small-prime correction is silently omitted.

Native pole neutrality gives integral_0^L exp(t)h_L(t)dt=-integral_0^L h_L(t)dt. Hence the deterministic term in(1) is
 integral_0^L h_L(t)dt + Prefix_L,
 Prefix_L=integral_0^b exp(t)h_L(t)dt.                    (2)
The lower prefix is generally nonzero and must stay. It is not an Arch term that may be set to zero.

sections.title: Complete prime-power counting returns the precise psi pairing
sections.proof:
Define the finite-at-every-t higher-power counting function H_J(t)=sum_(2<=r<=floor(t/b))pi(exp(t/r))/r and J(t)=Pi(t)+H_J(t). Thus J has an atom1/r at each actual p^r, retaining distinct powers and all their multiplicities. Put Delta_J=J-ell. Direct finite integration of its steps gives
 psi(exp t)=tJ(t)-integral_0^t J(u)du.
Similarly t ell(t)-integral_0^t ell(u)du=(exp(t)-2)1_(t>=b). Therefore the ACTUAL complete discrepancy is
 R_psi(t)=psi(exp t)-exp t
         =t Delta_J(t)-integral_0^t Delta_J(u)du-min(exp t,2).       (3)
Multiplying by h_L' and integrating, with both h endpoints zero, gives
 integral_0^L R_psi h_L'
 =Prefix_L+integral_b^L Delta_J(t)[t h_L(t)]'dt.          (4)
The term min(exp t,2) gives exactly Prefix_L. This verifies the lower correction without interchanging an unbounded prime series.

The extra counting term is exactly the unchanged higher-power contribution:
 integral_b^L H_J(t)[t h_L(t)]'dt
 =-sum_(p,r>=2,r log p<=L)log(p)p^(-r/2)k_L(r log p)
 =B_{>=2}(L).                                          (5)
The factor1/r in J is cancelled by t=r log p. Thus complete ordinary-prime partial summation plus the paid higher-power budget reconstructs the existing signed psi pairing. The original source, prime powers, native poles and full Arch compensation are all retained. Equations(3)-(5) add no new arithmetic assumption.

sections.title: An explicitly bounded compensated ordinary-prime remainder
sections.proof:
Use the frozen unconditional budget
 B_{>=2}=200a beta^2 L+d0 H2 L^2+r_hp, |r_hp|<=R_hp,
where H2=T2-8M1 and R_hp is the explicit fixed constant in that note. Its uniform jet has C_*=2^34 and
 |k_L(t)+d0 L^2 t^2|<=C_*(t^2+t^4), 0<=t<=L.
Since integral_0^infinity t^2 exp(-t/2)dt=16 and the fourth moment is768,
 integral_0^L h_L=-16d0L^2+r_h,
 |r_h|<=784C_*+768d0=:R_h.                              (6)
The truncated leading tail is paid by L^2t^2<=t^4 for t>L; no infinite tail is discarded.

Define the precisely compensated ORDINARY-PRIME expression
 E_ord(L)=B1(L)+200a(L)beta^2L+d0(H2+16)L^2.
Equations(1)-(6), or the complete psi identity, give the exact relation
 E_ord=integral_0^L R_psi(t)h_L'(t)dt-r_hp+r_h.            (7)
The full canonical gap remains
 G=J_det+E_ord+r_hp-r_h,
where the unchanged J_det=A_Gamma+integral_0^L h_L is the positive deterministic component from the companion note. Thus neither the Arch component nor its reflected continuum is omitted by the compensation.

Let P_e,P_o be the explicit nonnegative source polynomials from S2 of the frozen signed-psi baseline, and P_D=P_o+P_e. Since0<a<1 and L>=1, its exact growing-interval estimate gives |q_L'(v)+q_L(v)/2|<=L^(-7)P_D(v), q_L(v)=D_L(v/L), for ALL0<=v<=L. Classical quantitative PNT |R_psi(t)|<=C_psi exp(t-c sqrt t) then proves the actual unconditional bound
 |E_ord(L)|<=R_hp+R_h+C_psi I_D(c)L^(-7)exp(L/2-c sqrt L),
 I_D(c)=integral_0^infinity exp(-v/2+c sqrt v)P_D(v)dv<infinity.     (8)
The same PNT constant c is kept via sqrt L<=sqrt(L-v)+sqrt v. This is a paid signed estimate, but its remaining scale is exponential. The exact rational factor a(L) in the L^5 term is retained; replacing it by1/11 would leave an unpaid L^3 term.

sections.title: Why prime counting gives no extra logarithmic saving in this method
sections.proof:
For completeness, the ordinary-prime PNT estimate can be used directly in(1), rather than presuming a stronger counting error. Let E_theta(x)=theta(x)-x and suppose the already paid quantitative PNT bound |E_theta(x)|<=C_theta x exp(-c sqrt(log x)) for x>=2. Finite partial summation gives, for t>=b,
 Delta_pi(t)=E_theta(exp t)/t+integral_b^t E_theta(exp u)/u^2 du+2/b.  (9)
The +2/b is the actual lower endpoint; in particular (9) gives Delta_pi(b)=1. Splitting the integral at t/2 yields
 |Delta_pi(t)|<=C_pi exp(t-c sqrt t)/t,
 C_pi=C_theta[1+4J_c/b+4exp(c^2)/b^2]+4exp(c^2/2)/b,
 J_c=integral_0^infinity exp(-v+c sqrt v)dv<infinity.     (10)
For the lower half use t exp(-t/2+c sqrt t)<=4exp(c^2); for the upper half use u^(-2)<=4/t^2 and sqrt t<=sqrt u+sqrt(t-u). The same c is retained after including fixed constants.

But [t h_L]'=exp(-t/2)[t(k_L'-k_L/2)+k_L]. The leading t cancels the1/t in(10). If Q_e,Q_o are the corresponding explicit source polynomials bounding |E_p(L,v/L)| by L^(-r_p)Q_p(v), put Q_D=Q_o+Q_e. Since t>=b, the remaining q_L/t term is bounded by L^(-7)Q_D(v)/b. Thus the direct counting error has upper bound C_pi I_pi(c)L^(-7)exp(L/2-c sqrt L), with
 I_pi=integral_0^infinity exp(-v/2+c sqrt v)[P_D(v)+Q_D(v)/b]dv<infinity.
The extra counting denominator therefore does not yield another factor1/L or a smaller exponential rate. After the complete higher-power counting correction is included, the exact formula returns(7), not a separate independently small remainder.

sections.title: Positive matching asymptotic for the actual-source absolute envelopes
sections.proof:
This last assertion is a sharpness result for a SPECIFIED absolute-value proof method, not a bound from below on an actual prime discrepancy. Fix the PNT exponent c>0 and define the two actual-kernel envelopes
 M_psi(L)=integral_0^L exp(t-c sqrt t)|h_L'(t)|dt,
 M_pi(L)=integral_b^L exp(t-c sqrt t)/t |[t h_L(t)]'|dt.
The frozen native source expansion and its differentiated form give, uniformly on each compact v interval,
 L^7 q_L(v)->-C_o G7(v),
 L^7[q_L'(v)+q_L(v)/2]->-C_o H7(v),
 C_o=2(2pi)^6*240^2,
 G7(v)=v^7/7!-v^9/(2*9!)+v^11/(16*11!), H7=G7'+G7/2.
The even contribution is O(L^-2) after this scaling and a(L) stays bounded. H7 is a nonzero polynomial (its first term is v^6/6!), so the constant below is finite and strictly positive.

Change v=L-t. The tilted PNT ratio exp(c[sqrt L-sqrt(L-v)]) tends1 at fixed v and is at most exp(c sqrt v). The global polynomials P_D,Q_D already pay the ENTIRE growing range. In M_pi the extra q_L/(L-v) tends0 at fixed v and is globally bounded by Q_D(v)/b after scaling. Dominated convergence therefore gives BOTH exact limits
 M_psi(L)/(L^(-7)exp(L/2-c sqrt L))
 -> C_o integral_0^infinity exp(-v/2)|H7(v)|dv >0,
 M_pi(L)/(L^(-7)exp(L/2-c sqrt L))
 -> the SAME positive constant.                         (11)
The source half-moment cancellations do not annihilate this absolute integral. Equation(11) is actual-source evidence that the envelope bound used in(8)-(10) cannot itself be improved to a polynomial or to exp((1/2-delta)L) by relabeling prime counting. It does NOT show that the true discrepancy attains the envelope, that no other use of divisor/Selberg constraints helps, or that a signed cancellation estimate is impossible.

Comparison with history: the older signed-psi note already supplied the exponent1/2-c/sqrt L scale. New here are the exact PRIME-counting lower-prefix completion, its reconciliation with the explicit L^5/L^2 budget through a bounded remainder, and the matching positive majorant asymptotic for both counting methods. The previously checked divisor inversion and full Selberg identities transport the same source without a new lower bound. No independent noncircular closing supplier is obtained in this calculation; the remaining required information is signed cancellation of the actual discrepancy against this prescribed, aperture-dependent kernel.
